sentences.text: Yesterday our class sketched the green sea turtle, the one missing half a front flipper, for nearly an hour. The bus leaves at two, so we sprinted past the seahorse nursery, promising ourselves we'd come back. Copper sulfate concentrations must be verified twice daily with a calibrated test kit before any additional dosing occurs. Overhead in the acrylic tunnel, a sawfish slid by so slowly that the entire tour group fell silent. You raise the heat one degree every twelve hours, watching the thermometer, hoping the cories can handle the climb. My notes from week one read like a fever chart: spots up, appetite down, one tetra lost overnight. During the noon demonstration, an aquarist explained how target training keeps the sea lions engaged between meals. One kid kept squeaking a toy puffin by the registers until a clerk gently took it away. Interactive kiosks near the entrance quiz visitors on plastic pollution before releasing them into the shark gallery. Gift-shop chatter faded as we entered the darkened jellyfish gallery, all hush and drifting light. A diver in the big exhibit waved at the crowd, then hand-fed romaine to a grazing school of surgeonfish. Docents at this facility complete forty hours of training before they may lead a school group past the sea otter habitat. Behind the gift-shop register, plush hammerheads outsold the stingray magnets three to one during spring break. "Feeding demonstration at the kelp forest begins in five minutes," crackled the overhead speaker, and the whole hall shifted toward the amphitheater. One level scoop of kanamycin per five gallons, added right after the fifty-percent water change — never guess the volume. "No, don't double the dose," she told the panicked caller — "scaleless species absorb malachite green far faster than you'd think." Methylene blue stained everything in the isolation rack a deep cobalt, including my thumbnail and the airline tubing. On the phone, the aquatic vet talked me through netting the gourami, her voice low and steady the whole time. Those salt-grain specks scattered across the black molly? Classic ichthyophthirius, the parasite every hobbyist learns to dread. Have you ever watched a giant Pacific octopus unscrew a jar to get at its herring breakfast? Feeding time draws the biggest crowds; the sharks, oddly, draw the quietest ones. What is the meaning of the word tank?
